principles.text: Don't build until you know how to talk about it: find the one-liner you'd stop scrolling for, and decide the narrative first.
Judge launches by downloads and retention, not views. Virality means nothing if nobody keeps using it.
Charge from day one; a paying yes or no is higher signal than free usage.
Post short, unedited videos daily as a free lottery; traction likely comes around the 200th video, not the 10th.
Tell the world your progress consistently for 12-24 months, e.g. a weekly newsletter, and capital tends to find you.

sampleQA.question: How should I launch my product?

answer.text: Don't do one big launch. Ship raw mini demos as often as possible on algorithmic platforms.
Reuse one hook: who I am, what's going on, what I'm working on, then show it.
Track downloads and retention per channel (e.g. a dedicated link-in-bio), not views. Aim at the right niche, not virality.
For a launch event, set a deadline you can't move and a tiny goal, like 10 teams paying $99 a month.

sampleQA.question: How do I get my first customers?

answer.text: Get your first 10 to 100 customers offline by talking to real people before investing in social media.
Charge from day one. The best way to get people to pay is to charge.
Go where your ideal user hangs out. buildspace made custom landing pages for 20 college CS clubs.
When unsure, pull your top 25 users by usage, email 10 of them, and talk the next day.

sampleQA.question: Do I need a vision or a unique idea to start?

answer.text: No. Admit you don't know where you're going; vision is a skill earned by years of immersion in one craft.
There's no unique idea. Your execution is what makes your version feel different.
Ideas are forged, not found. Change yours a little every week and test it with the mom test.
